'''''Kalanchoe blossfeldiana''''' is a commonly cultivated [[evergreen]] [[house plant]] of the [[genus]] ''[[Kalanchoe]]'' native to [[Madagascar]]. It is known by the English common names '''flaming Katy''', '''Christmas kalanchoe''', '''florist kalanchoe'''<ref name="dave's garden">{{cite web|url=http://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/591/|title=Detailed information on Flaming Katy, Christmas Kalanchoe, Florist Kalanchoe Kalanchoe blossfeldiana|work=PlantFiles|publisher=[[Dave's Garden]]|access-date=6 December 2013}}</ref> and '''Madagascar widow's-thrill'''.<ref name="usda">{{cite web|url=http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=KABL |title=Plants Profile for Kalanchoe blossfeldiana (Madagascar widow's-thrill) |work=PLANTS Database |publisher=[[United States Department of Agriculture]]'s [[Natural Resources Conservation Service]] |access-date=6 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214072918/http://plants.usda.gov/core/profile?symbol=KABL |archive-date= 14 December 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Kalanchoe blossfeldiana'' is in the ''Kalanchoe ''section of the ''Kalanchoe ''genus, with a description of the plant published in 1934 (Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 35:159).<ref name="grin">{{GRIN | accessdate=12 December 2013}}</ref> Regarding the [[etymology]] of the binomial, Adanson adapted the [[genus#Generic name|generic name]] ''Kalanchoe'' from 'Kalanchauhuy', a [[Chinese language|Chinese]] name for one species recorded by [[Georg Joseph Kamel]], a botanist and Jesuit missionary to the [[Philippines]].<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/3611216#page/1076/mode/1up Adanson, M. Familles des Plantes]</ref><ref>Camel, J.G. Herbarium aliarumque stirpium in Insulâ Luzone Philippinarum Primariâ nascentium. In: John Ray: Historia plantarum. Band 3, London 1704, Anhang, S. 1–42 p. 6. item 18. [http://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/ing/Libro.php?Libro=3675&Pagina=817]</ref><ref name=AJB>{{Cite journal|title=Kalanchoe: The Genus and its Chromosomes| doi=10.2307/2436516|first=J. T.| last=Baldwin Jr.| journal=American Journal of Botany| pages=572–579| volume=25| issue=8| date=October 1938| jstor=2436516}}</ref> 

The [[Oxford English Dictionary]] states that it is "based on [the] Chinese 伽藍菜 [[:wikt:gāláncài|gāláncài]]",<ref name="oed">{{cite web|url=http://english.oxforddictionaries.com/definition/kalanchoe |title=kalanchoe |work=[[Oxford English Dictionary]] |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |access-date=12 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141214181017/http://english.oxforddictionaries.com/definition/kalanchoe |archive-date=14 December 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> whilst the [[Collins English |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212184237/http://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/kalanchoe |archive-date=12 December 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  The [[Botanical ==Description==
[[File:Kalanchoe blossfeldiana - flower view 01.jpg|thumb]]

''Kalanchoe blossfeldiana'' is a [[glabrousness (botany)|glabrous]],<ref name="plantoftheweek">{{cite web|url=http://www.plantoftheweek.org/week340.shtml |title=Kalanchoe blossfeldiana - Christmas Kalanchoe - Crassulaceae |last=Lemke |first=Carl |date=23 December 2005 |publisher=[[University of Oklahoma]] Department of Microbiology & Plant Biology |access-date=12 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130525072626/http://www.plantoftheweek.org/week340.shtml |archive-date=25 May 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> bushy, evergreen and perennial [[succulent plant]] which (in 2–5 years)<ref name="rhs">{{cite web|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1086 |title=Kalanchoe blossfeldiana AGM |work=Plant Selector |publisher=[[Royal Horticultural Society]] |access-date=6 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214081155/http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1086 |archive-date= 14 December 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> can reach an ultimate height of between {{convert|30|and|45|cm|in|abbr=on}}<ref name="dave's garden" /> and an ultimate spread of between {{convert|10|and|50|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}}.<ref name="rhs" /> ''K. blossfeldiana'' has a round [[Habit (biology)|habit]] and a moderate plant density; its growth rate has been described as 'slow'.<ref name="EDIS">{{cite web|url=http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/fp309|title=FPS-309/FP309: Kalanchoe Blossfeldiana Kalanchoe |last=F. Gilman |first=Edward |work=Electronic Data Information System |publisher=[[University of Florida]] |access-date=6 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211093205/http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/fp309 |archive-date= 11 December 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The plant has green,<ref name="rhs" /> shiny and textured glossy foliage<ref name="dave's garden" /> which stays green all year round.<ref name="rhs" /> The scallop-edged and ovate leaves are arranged in an opposite/subopposite fashion, are [[Simple leaf|simple in type]] with [[crenate]] margins and an oblong shape.<ref name="EDIS" /> The arrangement of the veins in a leaf ([[Leaf#Venation (arrangement of the veins)|venation]]) can be absent or very hard to see; the leaf blades are {{convert|5|–|10|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} long.<ref name="EDIS" />

Parts of ''Kalanchoe blossfeldiana'' are [[Poison|poisonous]] if [[ingested]].<ref name="dave's garden" />  

===Inflorescences=== 
''K. blossfeldiana'' flowers in late autumn to early winter; each flower has four petals and can be one of a wide variety of colours, from the dark reds and pinks to oranges, golds and whites. ''K. blossfeldiana'' is a short-day plant, meaning that its blooming cycle is regulated by the amount of sunlight it receives each day. The plant will bloom when it is receiving approximately 10 hours of daylight and 14 hours of darkness for 6-8 weeks.<ref>{{cite web |title=How to Get a Florist Kalanchoe to Rebloom |url=https://worldofsucculents.com/get-kalanchoe-rebloom/ |website=World of Succulents |date=1 October 2018}}</ref> The ovary is [[wikt:tetracarpellary|tetracarpellary]] and [[apocarpous]] while stamens are four in number and are [[wikt:epipetalous|epipetalous]].<ref name="dave's garden" /> The inflorescences are borne by [[peduncle (botany)|peduncle]]s which are higher up than the leaves and are [[:wikt:terminal#adjective|terminal]] in nature.<ref name="philippinemedicinal">{{cite web|url=http://stuartxchange.com/Kalancho.html|title=Kalancho/ Kalancho blossfeldiana / Christmas kalanchoe/ Flaming Katy |work=PHILIPPINE MEDICINAL PLANTS |publisher=STUARTXCHANGE |access-date=12 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402121018/http://stuartxchange.com/Kalancho.html |archive-date=2 April 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Kalanchoe blossfeldiana'' is native to [[Madagascar]], where the plant can be found growing in the relatively cool plateaus of the [[Tsaranoro Massif|Tsarantanana Mountains]]; ''K. blossfeldiana'' in this environment grows in [[humus]] soil.<ref name="plantsrescue">{{cite web|url=http://plantsrescue.com/kalanchoe-blossfeldiana/ |title=Plants & Flowers » Kalanchoe blossfeldiana |date=16 August 2013 |publisher=[[PlantsRescue]] |access-date=6 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212133615/http://plantsrescue.com/kalanchoe-blossfeldiana/ |archive-date= 12 December 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Ecology==
While generally disease-free, ''Kalanchoe blossfeldiana'' can be damaged by [[pest insects]] such as ''[[Otiorhynchus sulcatus]]'' (vine weevil) or [[mealybugs]].<ref name="rhs" />

==Cultivation==
With a minimum temperature of {{convert|10|C|F|abbr=on}}, ''K. blossfeldiana'' requires the protection of glass during the winter months in temperate locations. It needs to be in a cool, partially shaded spot. However, it may be placed outside in summer. In the [[UK]], it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/78810/i-Kalanchoe-blossfeldiana-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Kalanchoe blossfeldiana'' | access-date=13 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf 
| title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 56 | publisher = Royal HorticulturalSociety 
| access-date = 14 March 2018}}</ref>
